title: opportunistic-slo-buffer-and-circuit-snapshot-rollback
author: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring incidents where transient backend latency spikes caused long-lived circuit-open states in regional gateways. Those circuits were slow to recover because the in-memory circuit metadata missed short-lived fluctuations and some KV cache drains accelerated token debt, pushing SLOs over thresholds and triggering broad regional failovers. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an "opportunistic SLO buffer" that temporarily stalls aggressive eviction for very short windows when latency spikes are detected but error rates remain low, and (2) a circuit snapshot + rollback mechanism that can restore a recent healthy circuit state if the runtime detects a pathological stuck-open condition after a restart or leadership handoff.

What it does (summary): Adds a timed SLO buffer layer to the SLO enforcer that can be enabled per-region and per-traffic-class; implements a lightweight snapshot format for circuit state (open/closed counters, recent transitions, penalization buckets) persisted to the runtime's local durable store; exposes a controlled rollback API used automatically during node restarts or leader changes when recovery heuristics detect inconsistency. The combination reduces unnecessary failovers while preserving safety: the buffer is bounded and decays, snapshots are only used when checks guarantee monotonic safety.

Design notes: - Opportunistic SLO buffer: a short (configurable, default 5s) delay window where the enforcer holds off on increasing eviction severity when latency SLO breaches are spike-like and not accompanied by sustained error-rate increase or token-queue growth. The heuristic is: latency > latency_slo_threshold AND error_rate < error_rate_threshold AND kv_cache_fill_rate stable => start buffer window. The buffer decays with exponential backoff to favor eventual enforcement. - Circuit snapshot: on graceful leadership handoffs and regular checkpoints (configurable interval, default 30s) we serialize minimal circuit state to the local SSD store. On startup/handoff, the runtime compares persisted snapshot age and transition rate; if a circuit is open but snapshot shows steady closed history, we roll back to a safe closed-ish state with rate-limited probation. - Safety checks: snapshots are gated by signature and epoch; rollback only allowed if the node's epoch is ahead of snapshot epoch and health probes show stable egress.

Files changed (high level): - services/slo-enforcer/enforcer.go: implement buffer window logic and config knobs - services/slo-enforcer/probes.go: added probe hooks for buffer decision - runtime/circuit/state_snapshot.go: snapshot serialization, write/read helpers - runtime/circuit/rollback.go: rollback heuristics + probation state - cmd/opsctl/rollback_test.go: small integration test exercising snapshot/rollback - deployments/helm/values.yaml: feature flags and defaults - docs/operations/slo-buffer.md: operator-facing docs and emergency disable steps

Testing and safety: Unit and integration tests added for the heuristic boundaries, snapshot integrity, and rollback gating. Local canary run on perf-canary for two clusters (us-west-2a, eu-west-1b) for 48h with synthetic spike patterns; observed 43% reduction in automatic regional failovers for repeatable microbursts, and no increase in user-facing error-rate. We added a runtime metric redwood.slo.buffer.active and redwood.circuit.rollback.count for observability.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime feature flags; default OFF for existing clusters. Plan: enable in a 5% canary for two days, validate metrics and traces, then 50% for three days, then full rollout. Emergency disable via opsctl feature-toggle.disable slo-opportunistic-buffer.

Backout plan: If we see increased 5xx or sustained SLO degradation, flip the feature flag and optionally revert the migration commit. Snapshot files are written to a dedicated subdir and are never deleted immediately; ops can inspect/clear them.

Related: Linked Linear ENG-8421 (SLO resilience), ENG-8610 (circuit stability improvements).

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Local canary run - [x] Docs - [x] Metrics and alerts updated

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the buffer conservative (short by default) to avoid masking real systemic problems. The snapshot format is intentionally minimal to avoid coupling with future runtime semantics.

review_thread: Diego Ramos: The heuristics look reasonable; can you add an integration test that verifies we don't buffer when error_rate is high?
Aisha Nambiar: Added integration test simulating high error-rate path; buffer no-op verified (see cmd/opsctl/rollback_test.go).
Marta Chen: Two questions: 1) What's the expected disk usage for snapshots? 2) How does this interact with cross-region failover?

Aisha Nambiar: Snapshots are tiny (~1-2KB per circuit) and rotated; added doc section and metric redwood.circuit.snapshot.size. Cross-region: snapshots are strictly local and only used for local rollback; cross-region failover remains unchanged.
